boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Chicago, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence of campus landmarks, cultural stops, and student-facing spaces; confirm event availability before heading out.

cards.title: Start with the Campus Philanthropy Tour
cards.subtitle: Self-guided walk from Harper Memorial Library to Rockefeller Chapel
cards.notes: Download the self-guided tour, then use its thirteen narrated locations to orient yourself to the main quad at a comfortable first-day pace.
cards.short_summary: A 75-minute walking introduction to the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago describes this as a self-guided walking tour beginning at Harper Memorial Library, ending at Rockefeller Chapel, and taking about 75 minutes in person.
cards.access_notes: Use the Vamonde app as directed by the tour page; this is a self-guided outdoor route.

cards.title: Begin at Harper Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: 1116 E. 59th St.; the tour’s starting landmark
cards.notes: Meet your group outside the library and open the tour before setting off, so the first stop also gives everyone a clear shared route.
cards.short_summary: The documented starting point for UChicago’s campus philanthropy walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Philanthropy Tour begins in front of Harper Memorial Library at 1116 E. 59th Street.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor meeting point; follow the self-guided route from here.

cards.title: Pause at Botany Pond
cards.subtitle: Campus landscape landmark
cards.notes: Take a short, quiet loop around the restored pond and its bridge; leave wildlife undisturbed and keep the path clear for other pedestrians.
cards.short_summary: A restored campus pond with accessible views and new native plantings.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago reports that Botany Pond reopened after restoration with improved landscaping for universal access and views of the water.
cards.source_title: Botany Pond restoration revitalizes beloved campus landmark
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; use normal pedestrian paths around the pond.

cards.title: Step into Bond Chapel
cards.subtitle: Classics Quadrangle; near 1010 E. 59th St.
cards.notes: If it is open, enter quietly for a brief look at the small chapel, and defer to any session already in progress before lingering.
cards.short_summary: A small chapel in the Classics Quadrangle with weekday visitor access during session.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockefeller Chapel states that Bond Chapel is traditionally open 8:30 a.m.–4:45 p.m. Monday through Friday when the University is in session.
cards.access_notes: Traditionally open weekdays only while the University is in session; maintain quiet if a session is underway.

cards.entity_name: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Museum
cards.title: Explore the ISAC Museum galleries
cards.subtitle: 1155 E. 58th St.
cards.notes: Choose one or two galleries rather than rushing them all, then regroup outside to trade one object or detail each person noticed.
cards.short_summary: An archaeology museum with galleries spanning Egypt, Nubia, Persia, Mesopotamia, Syria, Anatolia, and the Levant.
cards.evidence_claim: ISAC identifies its museum at 1155 E. 58th Street and lists galleries devoted to Egypt, Nubia, Persia, Mesopotamia, Syria, Anatolia, and the Levant.
cards.source_title: Admission & Hours | Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures
cards.access_notes: Listed museum hours: Tuesday–Thursday and Saturday–Sunday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Friday 10 a.m.–8 p.m.

cards.title: See the Robie House
cards.subtitle: 5757 S. Woodlawn Ave.
cards.notes: Walk by the exterior for architectural context, or reserve a guided interior tour in advance if your group wants to go inside.
cards.short_summary: Frank Lloyd Wright’s Prairie-style house beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Frank Lloyd Wright Trust lists Robie House at 5757 S. Woodlawn Avenue and says entry is by guided tour only.
cards.source_title: Robie House Tours | Frank Lloyd Wright Trust
cards.access_notes: Guided tours run Thursday–Monday from 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; advance tickets are strongly recommended for interior entry.

cards.title: Finish the walk at Rockefeller Chapel
cards.subtitle: 5850 S. Woodlawn Ave.
cards.notes: Use the chapel as a final landmark for your first route across campus, checking visitor access before entering the building.
cards.short_summary: The documented endpoint of the campus philanthropy walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago’s Campus Philanthropy Tour ends at Rockefeller Chapel, and the chapel gives its address as 5850 South Woodlawn Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Traditionally open Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m.–1 p.m. when the University is in session; closed Mondays and Saturdays except special events.

cards.title: Listen for a carillon recital
cards.subtitle: Rockefeller Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Check the chapel calendar, then listen from the chapel viewing stations if a weekday recital aligns with your walk across the quads.
cards.short_summary: Live weekday carillon performances associated with Rockefeller Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Rockefeller Chapel says the carillon is played live in recitals at noon and 5 p.m. on weekdays when classes are in session.
cards.access_notes: Weekday recitals occur at noon and 5 p.m. when classes are in session; consult the chapel for current access status.

cards.title: Check the Ida Noyes Hall event board
cards.subtitle: 1212 E. 59th St.
cards.notes: Look for a campus event or student-organization gathering, then use the building as a planned rendezvous point rather than assuming a room is open.
cards.short_summary: A student-centered historic hall that hosts campus events and student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago Student Centers identifies Ida Noyes Hall at 1212 E. 59th Street and states its central goal is to provide facilities and services to student organizations and University departments.
cards.access_notes: Event rooms are used by student groups and departments; check the building’s schedule or event listing before relying on a specific space.

cards.title: Regroup at Reynolds Club
cards.subtitle: 5706 S. University Ave.
cards.notes: Use the Commons as a practical indoor regrouping stop, then choose a student-organization event or food option that fits your group’s plans.
cards.short_summary: A student-organization hub with dining options in the Reynolds Club.
cards.evidence_claim: UChicago’s pre-college welcome packet states that Reynolds Club includes the Hutchinson Commons food court, a Pret a Manger coffee shop, ATMs, and many student organizations.
cards.source_title: Pre-College Welcome Packet | University of Chicago Summer Session
cards.access_notes: Food and retail purchases are optional; availability can vary with the academic calendar.
